interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical diagram (combined diagram of the four elements, four qualities, four seasons, four winds or cardinal directions and the three continents)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram sets out a scheme of correspondences between macrocosmic orders. The four coloured circles IGNIS, AER, AQUA and TERRA stand for the four elements. Each is paired with two of the qualities CALIDYS, SICCYS, YMIDYS, HYMIDA, SICCA and FRIGIDA: fire is hot and dry, air hot and moist, water moist and cold, earth dry and cold. The four outer circles carry the names of the directions or winds: AUSER (south) at the top, HORIES (oriens, east) at the left, DE OCCINS (occidens, west) at the right and AQUILO (north) at the bottom. The orange bands joining these circles carry the seasons with their qualities: VER CALIDYM ET HYMIDYM (spring, hot and moist), AESTAS CALIDA SICCA (summer, hot and dry), and the two lower bands for autumn and winter. The lower left band reads HIEMPS FRIGIDYS HYMIDYS, an ordering that does not match the winter quality scheme exactly and may be a scribal or copying variant. The lower right band reads LHVMNVS SICCYS FRIGIDYS, probably AVTVMNVS, autumn, cold and dry. The inner T-shaped division into ASIA, AFRICA and EYROPA recalls the tripartite world map (T-O scheme). The whole diagram links the elements, qualities, seasons, winds and the known world in one harmonious macrocosmic structure inside a square frame.
interpretation.evidence: The labels IGNIS, AER, AQUA and TERRA, the quality words, the season names on the bands (VER, AESTAS, HIEMPS), the direction names (AUSER, HORIES, DE OCCINS, AQUILO) and the continent names ASIA, AFRICA and EYROPA are all transcribed in Step 1. The pairing of elements with qualities and seasons follows the standard medieval scheme of four elements, four qualities and four seasons. The band texts are hard to read in places. The reading of "LHVMNVS" as autumn is a conjecture. The Step 1 entries naming bands such as "HIEMPS FRIGIDYS HYMIDYS" and "LHVMNVS SICCYS FRIGIDYS" as objects of connected_to are uncertain, and the horizontal line is treated as connected to bands that it may only touch. The Step 1 entry linking the horizontal line to the bands is of low reliability. The Step 1 entry 'E AUS R' correctly reads the stacked letters of AUSER. Step 1 entries 10 and 12 use 'above' to relate circles to the quality labels; that relation is loose and the labels are better read as attributes of the elements. The dated sources and exact tradition (for example Isidorian or Bedan-type cosmological schemes) are not claimed here because they cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
